events.feedback:
Here is an analysis of your draft preview page for the Evening Bat (Nycticeius humeralis), broken down by content accuracy, accessibility/readability, engagement, and potential fun additions.

1. Fact-Checking & Technical Corrections
Native Flag & Keys Exclusion: The metadata flag note states "except the Keys". While rare in the Florida Keys, evening bats (Nycticeius humeralis) have occasionally been recorded in the upper/middle keys, though they are indeed absent or transient in the far lower keys. Clarifying "uncommon to absent in the Keys" is slightly more precise, though "except the Keys" is acceptable for a high-level summary.

Echolocation Peak Frequency: The text mentions a detector set to "25–35 kHz range". While evening bat echolocation pulses do sweep into that lower band, their peak frequency/maximum energy (Fmax) typically centers around 35 to 45 kHz (often ~38–42 kHz). Tweaking the suggested range to 35–45 kHz will prevent visitors using bat detectors from tuning too low.
